In addition, Your Honours, the Prosecution will not rely on the third sentence of paragraph 19. And then I have two issues to explain to the Trial Chamber related to the subject of translations. I had sent late last week 65 ter number 6530 to CLSS to be revised, to make sure that we'd have the best possible translation, and this is a document that Mr. Torkildsen quotes in paragraph 62 of his report. However, when I received the new translation yesterday, I noted that in a couple of lines -- well, in the first line of Article 1 of this exhibit and the last sentence -- or the last part of Article 2 of this exhibit, the newer translation slightly changes the word order, and so the effect of that is that the quotations at paragraph 62 of Mr. Torkildsen's report are now, in a sense, slightly inaccurate because they do not reflect the most recent translation. With your leave, when Mr. Torkildsen is testifying, I will take him to that paragraph, to that quotation, show him the recent translation, and ask him if that would change his opinions in any way. Second translation issue, Your Honour, relates to paragraph 118 of Mr. Torkildsen's report. At that paragraph Mr. Torkildsen quotes from 65 ter 532, which was a speech given by General Mladic at the 50th session of the National Assembly of the Republika Srpska on the 15th and 16th of April, 1995. And, indeed, Your Honour, I believe a portion of this exhibit was admitted through witness Mr. Baron van Lynden. Your Honour, the Prosecution realised last evening that the text that Mr. Torkildsen quotes at paragraph 118 does not come from a verbatim transcript -- excuse me, does not come from a verbatim translation of the B/C/S transcript of General Mladic's speech. Instead, it comes from a partial translation which Mr. Torkildsen believed at the time to be reflecting verbatim portions of Mr. -- General Mladic's speech. And, again, if you look at the verbatim English translation now for that entire speech, you will see that there are some differences between the verbatim translation and the quotation that Mr. Torkildsen provided in his report. So, again, with your leave, when Mr. Torkildsen is testifying, I will take him to that paragraph and show him the verbatim transcript, the verbatim translation, and ask if that would change his views at all. That is what I wanted to explain to the Chamber, Your Honours, before Mr. Torkildsen begins his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is there any comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should also like to say something for the record. I have been notified of this by Mr. Saxon, and for the time being I have no objection. He should go through all that with the witness. But I wish to correct the transcript a bit. He did tell me that there are differences in quotations during the break, and if it's only the differences in quotations, I do not mind that the matter be treated as Mr. Saxon suggests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I understand Mr. Lukic, yes, I was only referring to these small quoted portions at paragraph 118 of Mr. Torkildsen's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So you are not changing the report, you are changing the quotations by Mr. Torkildsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Effectively, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Effectively, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes -- thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Torkildsen is the next witness; however, I note it is 13:41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want us to postpone until tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think with only four minutes left, Your Honour, it makes the most sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will do so. We stand adjourned until tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of November, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.41 p.m.,
